Run by two people, so dishes can take a while (February–March 2026).
osaka_oishii_sake_nakayoshi_nipponbashi.notes: [Izakaya · a quiet sake-and-fish izakaya by Kintetsu Nippombashi] A calm 17-seat izakaya a minute from Kintetsu Nippombashi, run by two people, with fish the owner buys at the market and a deep drink list: over 40 sakes kept in a dedicated fridge, 80-plus shochu and 15-plus umeshu. Start with the sashimi platter, then the rolled omelet, brought out on a hot teppan with extra dashi poured on so it bubbles at the table. Diners also praise the fried hatahata, homemade zaru tofu, whitebait with grated daikon and ponzu, mackerel pressed sushi and monkfish liver with nara-zuke. Dishes can take a while, and one diner found many sakes out of stock. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Sake-and-fish izakaya run by two people (March 2026 review; Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: The owner buys seasonal fish at the market (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "It's served on a hot teppan, and just before serving, [extra dashi is poured] over it! The steam rises, and the dashi bubbles on the teppan…" — September 2026, Dashimaki.

"…every dish was delicious! I especially enjoyed the pressed sushi with mackerel and the tempura with aonori (seaweed) and onion. It's impressive that [it is managed] with just two people!" — March 2026.

osaka_keshiki_yakitori_higashishinsaibas.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; skewers come with house seasonings such as white wine sauce, escargot butter and black truffle oil (Tabelog listing), and tare is not described.

Phone reservations from Japanese mobile numbers only (Tabelog). Some items depend on supply (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Busy around 19:00, so book (October 2025). Opened 14 September 2019 (Tabelog).
osaka_keshiki_yakitori_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Yakitori · a 10-seat charcoal yakitori counter open to 5 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small counter yakitori bar near Shinsaibashi Station, open from 18:00 until 5 am, so it works for dinner or a 1 am second stop. More than 30 skewer cuts, many rare, come from Tanba chicken, Tokushima young chicken and Daisen Jidori, each grilled over charcoal, and some get unusual house finishes such as escargot butter or black truffle oil. The omakase is good value; add vegetable skewers, the garlic edamame and a comforting egg soup with thin noodles to finish. One diner found the duck tataki weaker than the rest. Reservations by Japanese mobile number only. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays; smoking allowed.

osaka_fukutaro_namba_dining_maison.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Fukutaro's department-store counter, Takashimaya 8F, Namba] The Takashimaya branch of Fukutaro, an okonomiyaki house whose main shop is nearby, on the eighth-floor restaurant level: a 15-seat counter where the cooks make each okonomiyaki on the teppan in front of you. The batter is fluffy enough to melt, the sauce measured; get the negiyaki with seasoned beef tendon, a mixed okonomiyaki or a buta-tama with a runny egg, and maybe squid yakisoba. Diners use it to dodge the queue at the main shop, though there's often a short line here too (orders are taken while you wait), and it takes time to cook. Takeout is popular. Weekdays it breaks between 14:30 and 17:00.

osaka_sumibi_kushiyaki_hinataya.notes: [Yakitori · a charcoal skewer bar for chicken and pork, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A casual charcoal skewer bar on the ground floor of GROOVE Shinsaibashi East, open from 16:00 to midnight, with an 8-seat counter that suits solo drinkers since skewers can be ordered one at a time. Alongside juicy yakitori it grills pork skewers and a spicy offal, and the soft-cartilage kara-age and doteyaki are worth ordering; one diner loved the sweet potato with honey mayo. Seasoning runs strong and rich, made for drinking, with ¥500 draft beer and highballs poured to the brim. A chopstick lottery comes with handwritten notes. Service opinions split: two diners found staff cheerful, two found them curt or pushy.

osaka_shu_shu_sake_bar_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Sake bar · a wood-toned sake bar with creative small plates, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A stylish fourth-floor sake bar in GROOVE Shinsaibashi East, warm wood inside, with a sake list that changes each visit, plus gin, shochu and whisky. The food is more than snacks: taro dumplings with beef and burdock in a nameko sauce, spring cabbage and prosciutto croquettes, Kagoshima chicken sashimi, fatty bluefin and seared mackerel, and in spring a run of firefly-squid dishes ending in clay-pot rice. The deep-fried house curry bread is a good take-home. Book a course for better value than ordering à la carte. Pretty sake cups and tableware. Rules: one non-alcoholic drinker per group, two-hour limit when busy. Closed Thursdays.

osaka_kogaryu_honten_amerikamura.notes: [Takoyaki · Amerikamura's 1974 takoyaki stand by Triangle Park] The original shop of Koga Ryu, a takoyaki stand across from Amerikamura's Triangle Park since 1974, now with about nine shops. Ten small balls come per serving, soft and gooey rather than crisp, with a strong dashi flavor and big pieces of octopus. One diner calls the classic sauce-and-mayo (¥600) the most popular; another was told that Koga Ryu was the first to put mayonnaise on takoyaki. The negi versions come buried under green onion, with sauce (¥700) or ponzu. Eat upstairs or take them to the park. Two diners say Osaka locals pointed them here instead of Dotonbori. PayPay or cash only.

osaka_naniwa_soba_namba_dining_maison.notes: [Soba · soba-shabu and meat dipping soba on Takashimaya's restaurant floor, Namba] The Takashimaya branch of Naniwa Soba, a small Osaka soba chain (four shops) on the seventh-floor restaurant level, with colorful seats. The signature, trademarked, is soba-shabu: Wagyu swished through the house dashi and eaten with fresh soba, as a course from ¥5,000. For a simpler meal, one repeat visitor always picks the meat dipping soba (¥1,300), pork in a lightly spicy chili-oil dip that becomes a rich soup when you add soba water at the end. Also chilled sudachi soba, ume-and-yam soba and an oyakodon set; diners praise the delicate Kansai-style broth. Open to 21:30 or 22:00, later than many department-store restaurants.

osaka_ola_tacos_bar_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Mexican · a late-night taco and tequila bar since 2001, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small Mexican bar near Shinsaibashi, open since 2001 and late into the night, with a neon 'Tacos' sign, a terrace and a Latin, clink-glasses mood. Tacos come on handmade tortillas: chorizo with tangy salsa, tender braised pork rib (¥880), pulled pork with beans, or cheese-filled. Start with the shrimp-and-avocado cocktail de camarón (¥1,320) and a crisp garlic-mushroom quesadilla. About 30 salsas sit ready for heat-seekers, and the tequila and mezcal list is deep; one diner who doesn't care for tequila found the tequila soda easy to drink. One diner found the chicken taco's mayo-like sauce unexpected. Book ahead: food can run out late. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Mexican taco and tequila bar (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Mexican food is about chili aroma and flavor more than heat (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Tacos on handmade tortillas; tequila and mezcal.

anecdotes.text: "Cocktail de Camaron (JPY 1,320, tax included) — Shrimp and avocado marinated with tomato and lime… Tacos de Costilla (JPY 880, tax included) — Tacos made with tender braised pork rib." — June 2026.
"The tacos were authentically delicious, featuring pulled pork and a bean paste, and the tortillas were especially tasty." — September 2026.

osaka_j_bowl_shinsaibashi.notes: [Café · thick açaí bowls and Greek yogurt in a bar-like room, Shinsaibashi] A small açaí-bowl and Greek-yogurt shop near Shinsaibashi Station with a dim, bar-like room and plush sofas. The açaí is thick and creamy, piled with fruit and honey, and you can build your own with granola, kiwi, coconut, nuts or mango; the Greek yogurt with comb honey is rich and filling. Bowls run about ¥1,680, which diners call a little pricey. Two diners called it the best açaí bowl ever, but one found a smaller, unripe-mango bowl on a return visit. Tabelog lists vegan options. Hours are unclear (the listing shows evenings to 4 am, reviewers came at lunch), so check before you go.

osaka_roco_pizza_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Pizza · a cheap oven-baked pizza bar, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small Italian-bar-style pizza place in the Higashi-Shinsaibashi drinking streets, known for cheap, chewy, rustic pizzas that are on the small side, so a group can order several. Diners like the Margherita, a basil pizza, the quattro formaggi with honey and a mentaiko pizza, with ahijo and prosciutto to start and inexpensive wine. There's a one-drink rule. Pizzas were ¥500–600 in older reviews; recent prices aren't reported. Service reports range from attentive (pizzas sent one at a time so each stays hot) to curt, and one diner found the backless stools hard going after an hour. Most reviews are older; the latest is June 2025.

chef_bio.background: Pizza and dining bar (Tabelog; 2018–2025 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Small oven-baked pizzas.

"The pizzas were about JPY 600 each, and we enjoyed authentic, oven-baked varieties. They were fluffy and delicious." — February 2020.

osaka_sushi_keyaki_shinsaibashi.notes: [Sushi · a quiet 8-seat Edomae counter near Amerikamura, Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, upstairs Edomae sushi counter of eight seats on the quieter edge of Amerikamura, open since 2014 and serving lunch as well as dinner. Each piece arrives already seasoned, with salt, citrus or plum paste instead of soy sauce. The ¥20,000 omakase runs like a small kaiseki: appetizer, three sashimi, grilled fish and chawanmushi before ten nigiri from squid and striped jack to chutoro, sea urchin and eel; there's also a ¥12,000 sushi course and lunch courses that diners call good value. Past highlights include tuna cooked in a salt crust, well-judged kohada and bonito with salt. You can ask for less rice. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.philosophy: Fish sourced each morning, seasoned piece by piece (Tabelog listing; April 2026).

osaka_teppan_dining_yo_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a calm wooden teppan bar off Amerikamura, Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A tidy, wood-lined teppan bar tucked away in Nishi-Shinsaibashi, a quiet alternative to the Dotonbori okonomiyaki queues. Okonomiyaki comes in several styles, pork, oyster, a mixed modern and even Hiroshima-style, served on individual pans; around it, yam-yaki, cheese tonpei-yaki, shrimp mayo, shrimp toast and a salty, well-liked soba-meshi, plus salt-grilled offal and thick beef tongue. One diner didn't care for the sauce. The owner, a woman, runs the kitchen alone, so it can be slow, but diners like the warm touches (a message card on the table, a candy on the way out) and fair prices. Tabelog lists vegan options; ask.

chef_bio.background: Teppan and okonomiyaki bar run by its owner, who cooks alone (September 2026 review; Tabelog). The owner, a woman, runs the kitchen alone, so service can be slow (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "I tried shrimp toast for the first time, which was like toast topped with shrimp chili, and it was delightful! The cheese tonpei-yaki was, as expected, delicious and paired perfectly with beer!" — September 2026.
"I had the mixed modern okonomiyaki as my main dish. Instead of being served on a teppan table, it came out on an individual frying pan-like plate." — May 2024.

osaka_yakiniku_en_ning_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Yakiniku · Ning's thick-cut green-onion tongue in a calm hotel-floor room, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] The second Higashi-Shinsaibashi branch of the yakiniku shop Ning, on the ground floor of an APA Hotel near Nagahoribashi: black-toned, calm, with a long counter and smokeless roasters. The thing to order is the thick-cut tongue wrapped in green onion, garlic and ginger, which the shop calls its own creation; grill it well. The Ning set (¥9,680) is a tour of 11 cuts, and the branch-only special misuji is worth adding. Also tongue yukhoe, yukhoe on gimbap and a gelato that surprised one diner with its quality. One diner had a grill that wouldn't heat on one side and found the beer too icy. 90-minute seating.

osaka_tempura_etsu_higashishinsaibashi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–22:00; closed Sunday and holidays, though it may open by advance booking; occasional irregular closures (Tabelog). A summer lunch was served in August 2026 (Tempura Gozen ¥1,650, ¥1,980 with shrimp). Dinner is a course, ¥12,100 including tax (August 2026). Reserve ahead (June 2026). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Non-smoking. BYO drinks allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_tempura_etsu_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Tempura · a 7-seat tempura course counter, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A quiet seven-seat tempura counter a few minutes from Shinsaibashi, where each piece is fried and handed over in front of you. The ¥12,100 dinner course opens with seasonal sashimi (steamed abalone with liver sauce, snow-crab sashimi), then light, crisp tempura, the shrimp especially juicy, with a fresh salad mid-way and a tempura rice bowl or tempura in tea broth to finish. In winter the showpiece is a female crab packed back into its shell and fried whole. Diners praise the warm, joking hospitality and a list of rare sake and wine. A summer lunch set ran ¥1,650–1,980 in 2026. Book ahead; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Tempura counter run by its owner-chef (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: The day's seasonal ingredients, seafood and regional vegetables (June 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Tempura course; whole fried snow crab.

anecdotes.text: "…the meat of the female crab was carefully extracted, placed back into its shell, and deep-fried whole. It was so exquisite that I hesitated to eat it." — June 2026.
"…the shrimp tempura stood out with its thin, crispy batter and juicy, plump filling… here it was surprisingly light…" — June 2026, course just over ¥10,000.

Children welcome; families with strollers are seated in a private room (Tabelog). Opened 6 April 2023 (Tabelog).
osaka_mahoroba_teppan_shinsaibashi.notes: [Teppanyaki · a relaxed teppan counter for Wagyu, lobster and abalone, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, grown-up teppanyaki restaurant in Higashi-Shinsaibashi with a six-seat counter and two private rooms, more relaxed than one diner expected. The chefs explain each ingredient and crack jokes while cooking, and the flames make for good photos. Black Wagyu is seared to your chosen doneness and cut, and one diner recommends wasabi; a fuller course adds Ise lobster and abalone, at about ¥24,000. Lunch runs about ¥3,000–4,000, and à la carte is possible when seats are free. Good for anniversaries: one diner got a surprise cake. Open daily, lunch and dinner.

chef_bio.background: Teppanyaki restaurant (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

"The meat, in particular, is perfectly seared on the outside while remaining tender and juicy on the inside… when paired with wasabi, the sweetness of the meat is enhanced even further." — September 2026.

osaka_mondial_kaffee_328_gut_wolf.notes: [Coffee · a roastery coffee bar by Yotsubashi Station, Minami-Horie] The roasting base of the small MONDIAL KAFFEE 328 group, a tiny coffee bar a minute from Yotsubashi Station where the big roaster sits in the room and the smell hits you at the door. Baristas brew single-origin hand drip to order; describe your taste (a strong brew suited one diner), or try the dark roast one diner saw many customers ordering. The café latte (¥600) and an amber, full-flavored iced Americano (¥600) are both praised. There's a chili con carne sandwich, a salad lunch (¥1,650 with a drink) and house-baked sweets. Five seats inside and five on the terrace, so it's often better as takeout. Beans for sale.

"I ordered an Iced Americano for JPY 600… At first glance, it may seem quite light, but the flavor and aroma are robust." — August 2026.

osaka_link_coffee_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Coffee · a quiet house-roasting kissa off the Shinsaibashi bustle, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, dim coffee shop just off the busy Higashi-Shinsaibashi streets, part Showa kissa and part mid-century American, with jazz playing and a counter for solo visits. It roasts its own beans and brews each cup to order: ask the owner for a recommendation (one diner was steered to a freshly roasted Mandheling), or try the mocha with its grapefruit-like acidity or the strong blend. The baked cheesecake is the standard partner, smooth and well balanced; coffee jelly is on the menu too. Not everyone was won over: one diner found the coffee ordinary, the dish-washing loud and the stay limited to 60 minutes. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: House-roasting coffee shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: House-roasted hand-brewed coffee; baked cheesecake.

"The atmosphere is a blend of a Showa-era Japanese café and mid-century American style. I ordered the Mocha Tamari. It had a subtle acidity reminiscent of grapefruit…" — December visit, April 2026 review.

osaka_fujimaru_higashishinsaibashi_portu.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the course includes cod croquettes, bread, a rice or risotto finish and an egg tart.

Reservations for the second floor only; often fully booked (September 2026). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Bottles from the shop downstairs can be opened upstairs for a corkage fee (September 2026). When full, the shop points to its sister restaurant RAINDROP near Tanimachi 4-chome (Tabelog).
osaka_fujimaru_higashishinsaibashi_portu.notes: [Portuguese · a Portuguese diner above a wine shop, near Nagahoribashi] Part of the FUJIMARU wine-shop group: downstairs a shop of about 1,000 wines and a standing bar, upstairs Casa da Andorinha, a long-running Portuguese restaurant that moved here from Honmachi. The ¥5,500 course is the way in: appetizers, crisp bacalhau croquettes, Tanba chicken piri-piri, a seafood cataplana, then rice or risotto to finish and a freshly baked pastel de nata. Two diners single out the octopus and the port wine, and you can pick a bottle downstairs and pay corkage. Staff are good at pairing wines. One diner missed Vinho Verde. It fills up, so book. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

osaka_banco_cafe_bar_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Café · an espresso café-bar from noon to 2 am, Amerikamura] A casual espresso bar on the north edge of Amerikamura, by the Hariju building, open from noon until 2 am and as much a day-drinking spot as a café. Order a double espresso, strong and well-roasted, or a cappuccino doppio, at prices one diner called cheap for a city café (¥363–583 in 2024). The homemade tiramisu, light and not too sweet, is the reason two diners came back; paninis and doria cover meals. Tables are well spaced and the style is laid-back: you're left alone. Smoking is allowed inside, there's no restroom, and one diner found the room getting cluttered. Terrace seats.

osaka_teppanyaki_kobe_monterey_grasmere.notes: [Teppanyaki · a 22nd-floor hotel teppan counter with a view, JR Namba] A teppanyaki counter on the 22nd floor of the Hotel Monterey Grasmere by JR Namba, with big windows looking west over Kyocera Dome toward Kobe, the Rokko range and Akashi Kaikyo Bridge. Courses move from small appetizers to seafood (live abalone grilled in front of you, Ise lobster, scallops), four seasonal vegetables, and black Wagyu with a choice of sauces and salts, then garlic rice or a rich black beef curry. Lunch courses are the value play; one long-time diner noted lunch prices have risen and the 80 g steak now feels small. Chefs are happy to chat. Closed Tuesdays.

anecdotes.text: "The fresh abalone was quickly grilled while still alive, served with its liver and an oriental sauce… We had sirloin cap and strip loin, served with garlic soy sauce, grated ponzu, and several types of rock salt." — June 2026, lunch course.
"It's unfortunate that due to rising costs, the price of the lunch special has increased… The 80g steak portion feels a bit small…" — October 2026.

cultural_comfort.note: Hotel counter; chefs chat as they grill (2026).

osaka_tempura_gosei_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Daily 18:00–24:00; irregular closures (Tabelog). Reservation only; call if running late (Tabelog). Please avoid strong perfume or hair products (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). English menu; sommelier on site (Tabelog).
osaka_tempura_gosei_shinsaibashi.notes: [Tempura · a 12-seat tempura and wine-pairing counter run by a couple, Shinsaibashi] A small, stylish tempura counter a minute from Shinsaibashi Station, run by a husband-and-wife team: one fries, the wife is a sommelier who pairs affordable wines and sake with each course. The meal opens with chilled kuzu somen sharpened with sudachi, then small seasonal dishes and uni piled on clay-pot rice before the tempura, which diners call light and gentle on the stomach. The standout is sweet shrimp from Amakusa with crisp fried heads; vegetables shine too. A rich curry is an optional finish. One repeat visitor keeps bringing guests to impress. Expect ¥15,000–30,000 with pairings. Reservation only; skip the perfume.

chef_bio.background: Tempura and wine counter run by two people, one a sommelier (September 2026 reviews; Tabelog). A husband-and-wife team runs the counter; the wife is a sommelier and chooses the pairings (September 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients with sommelier-chosen wines (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Tempura course with wine pairing.

anecdotes.text: "…the cold kuzusomen that came out first was absolutely perfect!… You must try the amaebi (sweet shrimp) here! The moment I took a bite, an incredible sweetness spread throughout my mouth…" — June 2026.
"I always feel that the tempura here is very gentle on the stomach… The wine pairing… was, as usual, outstanding." — September 2026.

osaka_kuromon_sushi_sakaba_kashin.gf_detail: Ask. Raw oysters and sashimi come with ponzu or soy; fried oysters and oden are also on the menu.

osaka_kuromon_sushi_sakaba_kashin.hours_raw: Daily 9:00–16:00; irregular closures (Tabelog; the listing blurb says from 11:00, and diners report being served from about 10:00). No cards or e-money; PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay and au PAY accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking on the ground floor; smoking only upstairs (Tabelog). Second-floor room bookable from two people (Tabelog). Children welcome (Tabelog). Takeout (Tabelog).
osaka_kuromon_sushi_sakaba_kashin.notes: [Seafood · a fair-priced seafood and sushi bar in Kuromon Market] The main shop of Kashin, a bright little seafood bar on Kuromon Market's main street that opens in the morning and welcomes a beer with breakfast. In a market known for high prices, diners single it out as fair: three big raw or grilled oysters for ¥999, tuna tekka maki for under ¥700, large scallops cut so you taste each part, fugu with ponzu, a five-kind sashimi platter and seafood bowls. Fried oysters and oden fill out the izakaya side. The owner buys fish daily and is cheerful company; staff are polite. It gets crowded, and the ground floor is cramped. No cards; QR payments only.

chef_bio.origin: Moved to Kuromon Market's main street in April 2021 (Tabelog listing); main shop of a small group with an Umeda branch (January 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Seafood and sushi izakaya with a staff-maintained Tabelog listing (Tabelog; 2023–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fish bought daily by the owner; the owner wants Kuromon to be more than overpriced food (January 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Oysters; bluefin tuna.

anecdotes.text: "3 Fresh Oysters for JPY 999… Three for JPY 999, and the same price for both raw and grilled is a great deal!" — October 2025.
"I heard that the owner of this restaurant strongly believes that Kuromon Market is not just about overpriced items!… Tuna Tekka – Amazing to get this for under JPY 700." — January 2026.

osaka_mugen_burg_namba.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–22:00 (last order 21:00); ends when the hamburg steak sells out; irregular closures (Tabelog). Weekday lunch special 11:30–15:00 (Tabelog). Bookings cancelled 15 minutes after the time (Tabelog). No cards or e-money; PayPay accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking, but the charcoal makes a lot of smoke, so the shop advises against visits by high-school-age guests or younger (Tabelog). English-speaking staff (Tabelog).
osaka_mugen_burg_namba.notes: [Hamburg steak · all-you-can-eat charcoal mini hamburgs, Namba] A Namba counter that serves bite-sized hamburg steaks grilled over charcoal, one after another, until you hold up the 'I'm satisfied' board, a hamburg version of wanko-soba. Choose a 30- or 60-minute course; rice, eggs for egg-over-rice, salad and a long condiment line (wasabi, yuzu pepper, grated daikon and ponzu, chili oil, a fierce hot sauce) are unlimited too. Diners say the hamburgs come crisp outside and juicy inside; one managed 20 in an hour. Note that once you stop, you can't restart, so pace yourself, and service can lag when the two staff are busy. Smoky. No cards; PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: All-you-can-eat hamburg steak shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Wanko-style charcoal hamburg steaks.

anecdotes.text: "The system here is that hamburgers keep coming until you show the board that says 'I am satisfied.'… once you stop, you cannot resume." — September 2026.
"With a variety of seasonings available, such as wasabi, yuzu pepper, grated ponzu, and chili oil, you can customize the flavors to your liking." — October 2026, 30-minute course.

Charge ¥300 per person, one-drink minimum (Tabelog). Over-20s only; heated tobacco only, no cigarettes (Tabelog). Cards and QR accepted; no e-money (Tabelog).
osaka_chuka_bar_jam_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Chinese · a 9-seat Chinese bar for mapo tofu, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A tiny Chinese bar in a converted snack-bar space in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, nine seats and open to 1 am, serving serious Chinese food with cocktail-bar style. The mapo tofu (¥1,200) is the signature, meaty, spicy and numbing; the beef-tendon version has its own fan. Also the yodare-dori, whose sauce one diner wanted to drink, grilled shumai of Jinan mochi pork (2 for ¥500), black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork, shrimp chili and seafood noodles in thick sauce. Pair with a Shaoxing highball or baijiu jasmine highball. The owner travels to research and source ingredients, and the room is friendly. ¥300 charge, one drink, adults only.

chef_bio.background: Chinese bar (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: The owner researches dishes and sources ingredients on trips (November 2025 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Mapo tofu; Chinese bar dishes.

anecdotes.text: "The Mapo Tofu was rich in meatiness, with a deep flavor, spiciness, and numbing sensation, all perfectly balanced… The sauce for the mouthwatering chicken was incredibly tasty!" — May 2026.
"…what takes it to the next level is the 'Beef Tendon Mapo Tofu.' I was amazed at how much more delicious it became with the addition of beef tendon." — July 2026.

osaka_kaminari_burgers_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Burgers · big Wagyu-and-pork burgers with crisp fries, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small second-floor burger shop near Shinsaibashi Station, known for thick, juicy patties of black Wagyu blended with domestic brand pork on a well-toasted bun, with a light sauce that lets the meat lead. The burgers are by a former French chef, mixing French technique into burgers. The burgers are big: some diners use a knife and fork, one prefers to wrap them in paper and bite. The fries get nearly as much praise, crisp with a refined sweetness; one diner called them the best fries ever. Get the Classic, the Comple, or the B set (¥2,500 with fries and a drink); a three-patty stack is there if you're hungry. Ten seats; it closes when the burgers sell out.

chef_bio.background: Burger shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The burgers are by a former French chef, mixing French technique into burgers (March 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Black Wagyu and pork patty burgers; fries.

anecdotes.text: "The combination of Japanese black wagyu and domestic brand pork creates an addictive masterpiece! The sauce is subtle, allowing the natural flavors of the meat to shine through." — March 2026, Kaminari Burger B set ¥2,500.
"They also have a monthly lottery, and if you bring a losing ticket, you can get a fried egg added to your meal…" — July 2026.

osaka_koryori_takuan_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · a hidden 5th-floor koryori for seasonal small plates and sake, Nagahoribashi] A calm Japanese room on the fifth floor of a building near Nagahoribashi, hard to find but often full, serving Osaka-style small plates with sake and shochu. The head chef trained at Naniwa Kappo Kameji in Nishi-Shinsaibashi. Dinner starts with a run of small dishes and a rich dashi that two diners single out, then a generous sashimi platter. The kitchen makes its own kombu salt for the rare chicken tempura, and the seasonal list runs from lightly boiled or fried conger eel and straw-grilled chicken to stuffed peppers with meat miso and spring rolls of whitebait and perilla. Finish with salted rice balls from an iron pot. Mostly à la carte, with courses too. Smoking allowed; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.philosophy: Seasonal ingredients; house-made kombu salt (June 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal small plates; sashimi; rare chicken tempura.

anecdotes.text: "'I make my own salt.' I instinctively stopped my chopsticks. The salt served with the chicken tempura was homemade." — June 2026.
"I especially enjoyed the homemade salted rice balls cooked in a cast iron pot that were highly recommended." — January 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 小料理 たく庵、大阪市中央区東心斎橋1-8-14 オーブナテ 5F、長堀橋駅から徒歩2分、月〜土18:00〜24:00、日曜休み、カードはAMEXのみ (以前は現金のみの案内も)、電子マネー・QR不可、喫煙可、18席 (カウンター6、4人テーブル3)、日本酒と焼酎にこだわり。口コミ(2026年1〜9月): ビルの5階でわかりにくいが満席が多い、最初の小鉢とだしがおいしい、sashimi の盛り合わせ (炙りかんぱち、昆布の鯛、明石のタコ、イトヨリ、穴子、イカ、shirasu)、自家製の昆布塩で食べる鶏のレア天ぷら、とうもろこしの天ぷら、穴子の湯引き、穴子と秋茄子の揚げ物、shirasu と大葉の春巻き 酒粕ときのこのソース、藁焼きの鶏、ピーマンの肉味噌詰め、豚巻きの Manganji とうがらし、鰻の肝焼き、和牛のたたき、鉄鍋で炊いた塩おにぎり、冬はshirako や牡蠣のポン酢、日本酒の飲み放題コースのイベントも。

osaka_wagyu_steak_shibaraku.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Wagyu steak restaurant.
osaka_wagyu_steak_shibaraku.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–23:00 (food last order 22:00); irregular closures (Tabelog). Opened 16 December 2025 (Tabelog). Reservations cancelled 15 minutes after the time (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Non-smoking. English digital menu; children welcome (Tabelog). Rice refills free (May 2026).
osaka_wagyu_steak_shibaraku.notes: [Steak · lean Wagyu steak with premium rice, near Nagahoribashi] A counter steak restaurant near Nagahoribashi, opened December 2025, built around a simple pairing: lean black Wagyu, cut into bite-size pieces, and rice chosen to go with it. The lean 200 g set (¥3,960 in May 2026) comes tender and juicy, with free rice refills, a small beef-tendon curry good enough to stand alone, kimchi and miso soup; add sirloin cap if you want more fat, and try the grated wasabi. Two diners are already repeat visitors. Open 11:00–23:00, so it works for a late lunch. One diner found the staff chatted among themselves a bit much.

No reservations; weekend waits of 20–60 minutes, with sun umbrellas lent to the queue (September–October 2026). Cards, e-money and QR (PayPay) accepted (Tabelog; October 2026). Non-smoking. English menu and English-speaking staff (Tabelog; 2026). Children welcome (Tabelog). Opened 8 May 2013 (Tabelog).
osaka_west_wood_bakers_minamihorie.notes: [Café · a queue-worthy American breakfast café in Minami-Horie] A warm, wood-and-vintage American bakery café among the Horie fashion shops, open for breakfast and lunch since 2013, with a line on weekends. The pancakes are the draw: thin, flavorful, piled with bacon and eggs and plenty of maple syrup (¥1,250). The croque madame on the house natural-yeast bread (¥1,485) makes a hearty breakfast, and the burgers, such as avocado and mozzarella, come with crisp fries; one diner didn't care for the thick truffle fries. Donuts appear only on weekends and holidays. Arrive at 9 am on a weekday to skip the wait; at weekends expect 20–60 minutes.

anecdotes.text: "…the pancakes, which were the most popular item, were so delicious… They came with bacon and eggs, drenched in plenty of maple syrup…" — October 2026, BACON & EGG PANCAKES ¥1,250.
"I ordered the homemade natural yeast bread Croque Madame breakfast set for JPY 1,485. The bread had a chewy texture, paired with soft ham and rich eggs…" — October 2026.

osaka_kushiyakitei_honten_namba.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; skewers are seasoned on the teppan, and sides include spring-roll dumplings, mini okonomiyaki and tonpei-yaki.

Reservations on weekday evenings only (Tabelog). Charge ¥300 per person (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Children welcome (Tabelog). Two hours free at the Times car park west of Takashimaya with ¥3,000 spent (Tabelog). Opened 1 November 2017 (Tabelog).
osaka_kushiyakitei_honten_namba.notes: [Kushiyaki · teppan-grilled skewers on Takashimaya's restaurant floor, Namba] A kushiyaki restaurant on the eighth floor of Takashimaya's Namba Dining Maison, where skewers of meat, seafood and vegetables are grilled on a teppan and served on the plate: pork-wrapped asparagus, Wagyu, enoki rolled in meat, shrimp paste, tsukune, plus a monthly limited menu. Lunch is the easy way in, from an omakase of nine skewers to an Osaka course with mini okonomiyaki and a teppan rolled omelet (the omelet set was ¥1,800 in July 2026; one diner found five skewers on the light side). At dinner, add tonpei-yaki and a punchy garlic fried rice. Reservations on weekday evenings only.

chef_bio.specialty: Teppan-grilled kushiyaki skewers.

anecdotes.text: "The skewers, carefully grilled on a teppan, not only bring out the rich flavors of the ingredients but are also seasoned perfectly… the garlic fried rice we ordered was exceptionally tasty." — June 2026.

osaka_stand_catenaccio_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Bar · a Japanese-Italian standing bar to 3 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A basement bar near Shinsaibashi Station that ran for years as a meat-sushi and Italian bar and reopened in September 2026 as a standing bar, same chef and team, with the counter stools gone and two tables kept for groups. The menu now mixes Japanese and Italian: beer-battered zucchini fritters with charcoal salt, lobster cream spring rolls showered with Grana Padano, duck carpaccio, crab pasta, small plates like chilled tofu with caviar, and caramel pudding. One September 2026 diner reports the meat sushi was dropped in the renewal. A short but good sake list. Open until 3 am; smoking allowed.

osaka_paname_crepes_de_paris.notes: [Crêperie · Parisian crepes and galettes behind Hotel Nikko, Shinsaibashi] A stylish little crêperie behind the Hotel Nikko in Shinsaibashi, with a Paris-styled room and pretty tableware, open from 10 am to 11 pm. A review says the crepes are made by a French chef. The savory side draws the warmest reviews: a Salmon Royal galette loaded with salmon and rich cheese, and a juicy, slightly spicy minced-meat one, both big enough for dinner. Sweet crepes are chewy with crisp edges, from a simple sugar-butter-lemon to chocolate with lightly sweet cream; one diner found the Dubai chocolate too sweet to finish. Eating in requires one drink each, and payment is cashless only. Tabelog lists vegetarian options.

osaka_agetenka_kushikatsu_honten.notes: [Kushikatsu · light-batter kushikatsu and oden to 2 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small, lively kushikatsu counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open until 2 am, where skewers are fried in front of you in a thin, crisp batter that stays light enough to keep ordering. Diners pick out the Wagyu, the angel shrimp, whiting, Camembert and a marinated tuna skewer, dipped in the house sauce, with the shop's frozen lemon sour alongside. Unusually, there's a good oden pot too. Expect ¥4,000–8,000 with drinks. Diners praise the friendly staff and the owner's sunny manner, though one found orders missed and the bill wrong on a busy night. Smoking allowed.

osaka_kasumiya_nagahoribashi.notes: [Izakaya · a hidden chicken-and-beef izakaya with ¥1,000 lunches, Nagahoribashi] A small izakaya tucked at the very back of a dining building by Nagahoribashi Station, with a cozy, folk-tale feel and a semi-private nook. At lunch it serves set meals around ¥1,000: kara-age that one long-time diner says has improved (thinner coating, now with tartar sauce), a kara-age and offal set, and a well-seasoned fish set with plenty of sides; in 2025 it briefly ran a curry-only lunch from ¥600. At night it's chicken and beef tongue with drinks, and one diner happily stayed two hours. Tables are small and smoking is allowed. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.specialty: Kara-age lunch; chicken and beef tongue.

osaka_kogen_chinese_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Chinese · a one-person Chinese counter with cheap, generous plates to 1 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A 12-seat Chinese counter near the Crysta Nagahori stairs, run by one person who cooks fast and well, open until 1 am. Prices are low and portions generous: spicy yodare-dori for ¥450, big-shrimp chili for ¥790, a seafood stir-fry loaded with squid, scallops and shrimp (¥850, the priciest dish), and almost-always-on boiled dumplings, six for ¥450. A weekly blackboard adds things like sweet-and-sour chicken with lettuce. One diner made eight visits. Two or three dishes fill one person, so it's better shared. The shutter often looks half-closed even when open, and the owner may smoke when it's quiet.

osaka_toriyaki_sakaba_akatsuki.notes: [Chicken izakaya · chicken sashimi and off-the-skewer yakitori in private rooms, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm chicken izakaya two blocks east of Shinsaibashi-suji, with private rooms and bamboo-blind booths that suit groups. It serves chicken sashimi from Kagoshima chicken (¥1,980 for an assortment), horse sashimi, and yakitori grilled and served off the skewer, which means less smoke on your clothes. Highlights diners name: the cheese tsukune with egg yolk, lemony chicken neck and asparagus, an aged grilled thigh, and the green-onion-salt beef tongue fried rice the owner recommends (¥980). A truffle egg-over-rice and big grilled rice balls are other ways to finish. Good sake and shochu; courses for parties. Closed Wednesdays.

osaka_kanjang_gejang_watari_shinsaibashi.notes: [Korean · soy-marinated crab courses in private rooms, Nagahoribashi] A fifth-floor Korean restaurant by Nagahoribashi Station built around ganjang gejang, raw blue crab marinated in soy sauce, served in quiet private and semi-private rooms (some with sunken kotatsu). The crab is sweet and creamy, good with rice; soy-marinated shrimp comes with lemon. Courses (about ¥6,980) add namul, japchae and jeon, and the nakopsae seafood hot pot ends with noodles under egg yolk, cheese and pepper. A rare-sake list fits the Japanese-leaning seasoning. One diner found portions smaller than expected, and another was hurried out at a two-hour limit nobody had mentioned, so ask when booking.

The signature is grilled duck soba in a rich, sweet broth with plenty of Kujo green onion. Every set meal comes with steaming clay-pot mixed rice you can refill, plus house pickles and free tempura bits, and the custom is to finish the rice ochazuke-style with soba broth or tea. The eel mixed-rice set (¥2,100) is a treat; most sets are about ¥1,800, which one diner found steep for a casual lunch. Expect a short line at weekends. Closed Wednesdays.

osaka_futahako_kashimin_uranamba.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Kishiwada-style kashimin-yaki and late drinks, Ura-Namba] A narrow, counter-only bar in Ura-Namba, the second shop of a kashimin-yaki specialist, serving the Senshu cousin of okonomiyaki that's rare in central Osaka. The owner is Nakagawa of the comedy duo Randies, who still serves customers, and the walls are covered with comedians’ autographs. A thin crepe is topped with crunchy cabbage, little pieces of chicken and minced beef fat, which melts into the batter for a rich but surprisingly light cake; the original is ¥650, so groups order several (green onion, cheese curry, mochi and cheese). Also the hefty western-style modern with noodles, a garlicky udon-soba-offal 'uso-yaki', soba-meshi with natto and good drinking snacks. Open to 2 am; no cards; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.origin: Second shop of the kashimin-yaki specialist Hako (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The base is a crepe with plenty of crunchy cabbage, and the batter poured in creates a wonderfully gooey finish. The minced meat is grilled to perfection, and the chicken adds a delightful crunchy texture." — December 2024, Kashimin-yaki original ¥650.
"The amount of batter is minimal, and the seasoning is very rich, making it perfect to enjoy with beer!" — November 2025.

osaka_cafe_hapje_kitahorie.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–18:00 (food last order 17:30) (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Children and strollers welcome; takeout; outlets and Wi-Fi (Tabelog). Opened 15 May 2016 (Tabelog).
osaka_cafe_hapje_kitahorie.notes: [Sweets · crisp Brussels waffles baked to order, by Yotsubashi] A small café a minute from Yotsubashi Station that bakes Brussels-style waffles to order, with unsweetened batter, Belgian butter and Belgian chocolate and toppings. They come out crisp and light rather than chewy; the plain one with powdered sugar (¥600) is the purist's choice, and the seasonal plates go big, like a chilled sweet-potato brûlée (¥1,400). Pick your chocolate, or add pudding and vanilla ice cream. An espresso shake (¥600) surprised one diner as the highlight. One found the cream ordinary. Comfortable for families, with sofa seats; open 10:00–18:00 daily.

chef_bio.background: Belgian-waffle café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredients from Belgium; unsweetened batter with Belgian butter (Tabelog listing).

"I had the Chilled Sweet Potato Brulee Waffle for JPY 1400 and the Espresso Shake for JPY 600… I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious the Espresso Shake was…" — October 2026.

Takeout (Tabelog).
osaka_oh_oui_oui_minamihorie.notes: [Coffee · a specialty coffee café where you pick your cup, Minami-Horie] A small, decorated café in Minami-Horie that takes coffee seriously: single origins sorted into dark and fruity, each about ¥999, with staff happy to explain light roasts and match a bean to your taste. You choose your own cup and saucer from the shelf (fine porcelain, one diner noted), and any coffee that doesn't fit is served on the side. Diners single out an Ethiopian for its balance of aroma and acidity and an Indonesian 'dark' that drinks clean with chocolate notes. Ordering can be slow when it's busy. Dog-friendly. Cash only; open until 23:00 on weekdays.

chef_bio.background: Specialty coffee café (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Single-origin specialty coffee.

anecdotes.text: "If you choose to enjoy your coffee inside, [you can] pick your favorite cup. If the smaller cup can't hold all the coffee, [the extra is served] separately…" — April 2026, Indonesian ¥999.
"The specialty coffee from Ethiopia left a strong impression on me… the balance of aroma and acidity in the coffee was truly remarkable." — November 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 堀江カフェ オー ウィ ウィ、大阪市西区南堀江1-15-17 101、四ツ橋駅・桜川駅から徒歩5分、平日10:00〜23:00、日・祝10:00〜19:00、不定休、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、禁煙、20席、ペット可、テイクアウト。口コミ(2025年4月〜2026年10月): スペシャルティコーヒーをダークとフルーティーに分けて、エチオピア、ブルンジ、インドネシア、1杯999円ほど、好みを伝えると選んでくれる、浅煎りの説明が丁寧、カップとソーサーを選べる、入りきらない分は別に、店先の飾り、朝は開店待ちも、混むと注文に時間がかかる、犬連れ可で木の床なので小型犬はマットを。

osaka_m_and_h_coffee_kitahorie.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: bagels with ham, bacon, egg, salmon and cream cheese; milk lattes; nothing described as vegan.
osaka_m_and_h_coffee_kitahorie.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 8:30–16:30; Saturday–Sunday 8:30–17:00 (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Eat in: order at the table and pay on leaving; takeout: order and pay at the register (February 2026). Nearly full one Saturday afternoon (June 2026).
osaka_m_and_h_coffee_kitahorie.notes: [Café · an early-opening surf café for bagels and lattes, Kita-Horie] A small, surf-themed café near Yotsubashi that opens at 8:30, rare for the area, with a feel one diner compared to being abroad. The owner speaks English. Breakfast and lunch are bagel sandwiches packed with fillings (bacon, egg and cheese ¥980; ham and avocado; salmon, prosciutto and cream cheese), messy but filling; one diner found the bagel itself a bit hard. Coffee is hand-dripped from three beans, ground per cup, and takeaway cups get a hand-drawn illustration. The lattes stand out, especially a thick caramel latte; sweets include a tiramisu on a waffle base. Cramped inside, and it can be nearly full on weekend afternoons.

chef_bio.background: Café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner speaks English (June 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Bagel sandwiches; lattes; hand-drip coffee.

anecdotes.text: "I was delighted to see [the beans ground] on the spot and [each cup] carefully drip[ped]… The take-away cup came with a hand-drawn illustration…" — February 2026, Indonesian hand drip.
"It was much richer and creamier than I had imagined, and the milk was delicious... it paired perfectly with the caramel." — February 2026, caramel latte.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: M&H COFFEE、大阪市西区北堀江1-4-11 1F、四ツ橋駅から136m、月〜金8:30〜16:30、土日8:30〜17:00、カード・電子マネー・QR可、14席。口コミ(2026年2〜10月): 朝早くから開くカフェ、サーフ風の店内、ベーコン・卵・チーズのベーグル980円、ハムとアボカド、サーモン・アボカド・生ハムとクリームチーズ、具だくさんで食べにくいという声、ベーグル自体は固めという声、3種の豆から選ぶハンドドリップ (その場で挽く)、テイクアウトのカップに手描きのイラスト、キャラメルラテ、バニラ抹茶ラテ、金木犀のラテ、ワッフル生地のティラミス、温かいさつまいものケーキ、チョコのチーズケーキ、オレンジジュース550円、パイナップルジュース、ビール、グッズ、店内は席で注文して帰りに支払い、持ち帰りは先にレジで、土曜の午後にほぼ満席だったという声。

osaka_tera_cafe_chaniwa_minamihorie.hours_raw: Thursday and Friday 12:00–17:30 (last order 17:00); Saturday 11:00–17:00 (Tabelog listing); closing days may vary. Cash only (Tabelog; March 2026). Non-smoking. Children and pets welcome; kids menu (Tabelog). Opened 1 April 2017 in a corner of Banpukuji temple (Tabelog).
osaka_tera_cafe_chaniwa_minamihorie.notes: [Café · a temple café overlooking a garden, Minami-Horie] A calm café tucked into a corner of Banpukuji, a roughly 400-year-old Jodo Shinshu temple in Minami-Horie, open only Thursday to Saturday. Window seats look straight onto the tended temple garden. The sweets are made in-house: a daily sweets set (¥1,650) such as a rich cheesecake with caramel and almonds, or a seasonal wagashi tray of red bean, chestnut, ice cream and chrysanthemum monaka, good with the properly made matcha. Summer brings an ume-syrup kakigori topped with a pickled plum. Prices run high for drinks (matcha about ¥1,400), which one diner put down to the view. Cash only.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 1 April 2017 inside Banpukuji, a Jodo Shinshu Honganji-sect temple (Tabelog; July 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Temple café (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Original Japanese sweets by an in-house patissier (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal sweets sets with matcha.

anecdotes.text: "The cheesecake was rich and creamy, topped with a strong caramel sauce and almond slices that enhanced its flavor." — July 2026, Today's Sweets Set ¥1,650.

"On the tray, there was a delightful array of sweet red bean paste, chestnuts, ice cream, and adorable chrysanthemum-shaped monaka and wagashi!… the authentic matcha was simply outstanding!" — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 寺cafe & Live 茶庭、大阪市西区南堀江1-14-23、四ツ橋駅から徒歩6分、Banpukuji の一角、毎週木・金12:00〜17:30 (L.O. 17:00)、土11:00〜17:00、休みは変わることも、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、禁煙、20席、テラス、子ども・ペット歓迎、キッズメニュー、2017年4月1日開店、パティシエのオリジナルの和菓子、公式サイトあり。口コミ(2025年11月〜2026年10月): Jodo Shinshu の約400年の寺、窓から手入れされた庭、本日のスイーツセット1,650円 (キャラメルとアーモンドのチーズケーキ)、季節の和菓子セット (あんこ、栗、アイス、菊の形のmonaka )、抹茶約1,400円、抹茶ラテ、ほうじ茶ラテ、コーヒー550円、アイスカフェラテ700円、夏は梅干しをのせた梅シロップのかき氷、写真の「メニュー（かき氷）」、ドリンクは高めという声、現金のみ。

osaka_naniwa_korishitsu_kitahorie.hours_raw: Summer only: open roughly 12:00 (12:30 on weekdays per one review) to 18:00 daily in season; closed on rainy days; the 2026 season ended 23 September, so it is closed until next summer (Tabelog; September 2026). osaka_naniwa_korishitsu_kitahorie.notes: [Shaved ice · a summer-only old-style kakigori stand, Yotsubashi] A long-running ice shop by Yotsubashi Station that sells kakigori only in summer, shaved from big clear blocks into a fluffy pile that doesn't bring on brain freeze, then soaked through with syrup. A cup is ¥360 (strawberry, melon, Hawaiian Blue, or lemon with house-made syrup), and milk adds ¥100, so you still get change from ¥500. There's just a three-person bench; many eat standing on the pavement, often with families and a short line on hot afternoons. It closes on rainy days. The 2026 season ended on 23 September; check again next summer. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Long-established ice shop open in summer (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Old-style kakigori.

anecdotes.text: "In a world where desserts often exceed JPY 1,000, this fluffy kakigori is available for just JPY 360." — August 2026.
"Using pure ice, it's less likely to give you a brain freeze and has a fluffy texture." — September 2026, Strawberry ¥360.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 浪速氷室、大阪市西区北堀江1-11-3、四ツ橋駅6番出口から徒歩1分、12:00〜18:00、雨の日は休み、夏季のみかき氷、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、禁煙、3人がけのベンチ、テイクアウト。口コミ(2026年8〜9月): 夏だけの昔ながらの氷屋、大きな透明の氷を細かく削る、ふわふわで頭がキーンとなりにくい、1杯360円 (いちご、メロン、ハワイアンブルー、自家製シロップのレモン)、ミルク追加100円で500円でおつりがくる、レモネード、歩道で立って食べる、暑い午後は短い行列、家族連れも多い、写真に「今度はいちごにミルク増量しよかな」、2026年の営業は9月23日で終了。

osaka_mame_runrun_nambanaka.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 8:00–18:00; closed Monday; may change (Tabelog). Order and pay at the register, then sit (October 2025). Cards and QR (PayPay, d Barai, au PAY) accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Children and strollers welcome; takeout (Tabelog). Opened 20 November 2023 (Tabelog).
osaka_mame_runrun_nambanaka.notes: [Café · a Taiwanese-style soy milk café for breakfast, Namba] A cheerful little café near Edion Arena decorated with cartoon soybeans, serving soy milk made the Taiwanese way: lighter and more refreshing than Japanese soy milk, with a stronger bean taste. Choose plain, oolong-tea, black sesame or mixed berry (¥660), and set the sweetness level yourself; one diner found 25% just right. A fluffy, juicy Taiwanese meat bun (¥320) makes it breakfast, and the bun-plus-soy-milk combo was ¥500. Summer adds shaved ice with tapioca, and you get sunflower seeds to crack while you sit. Opens at 8:00; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Soy milk café (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Taiwanese-style soy milk (October 2025 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Taiwanese soy milk; meat buns.

anecdotes.text: "I opted for no added sweetness, allowing the gentle sweetness and tartness of the berries to blend smoothly with the soy milk…" — October 2025, Mixed Berry Soy Milk ¥660, Meat Bun ¥320.
"I had the Taiwanese meat bun and soy milk, and I was amazed that it only cost JPY 500." — June 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 豆ルンルン、大阪市浪速区難波中3-4-40 南大阪ビル 1F、南海なんば駅から徒歩5分、火〜日8:00〜18:00、月曜休み、カード・QR (PayPay・d払い・au PAY) 可、電子マネー不可、禁煙、12席 (テーブル8、カウンター4)、子ども・ベビーカー歓迎、テイクアウト、2023年11月20日開店。口コミ(2025年8月〜2026年6月): 台湾式の豆乳の店、豆のキャラクターのかわいい店内、エディオンアリーナの近く、プレーンの豆乳 (ホット・アイス)、烏龍茶の豆乳、黒ごまの豆乳、ミックスベリーの豆乳660円、甘さを選べる (25%がちょうどいいという声)、台湾の肉まん320円、肉まんと豆乳で500円、夏はタピオカのかき氷、ひまわりの種のサービス、レジで注文して席へ、もう少しコクがほしいという声も。

osaka_wacaron_waka_kitahorie.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: dorayaki-style pancake wrappers around cream, red bean paste and mochi; no gluten-free item described.
osaka_wacaron_waka_kitahorie.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: cream, custard and cheese-cream fillings; nothing described as vegan.
osaka_wacaron_waka_kitahorie.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 11:00–18:00; closed Wednesday; may change (Tabelog). Mainly takeaway; four counter seats listed, and one diner ate on a bench by the door (Tabelog; May 2026). Wacaron are handed over frozen and thaw to eating temperature (May–August 2026). Cards and QR accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Opened 10 September 2020 (Tabelog).
osaka_wacaron_waka_kitahorie.notes: [Sweets · fresh-dorayaki 'wacaron' and mitarashi rolls, Kita-Horie] A small Japanese-sweets shop near Yotsubashi that turns dorayaki into 'wacaron': thin, soft pancakes sandwiching a thick layer of cream in flavors like blueberry cheese (¥480), custard, or matcha and hojicha with red bean. They're handed over frozen and soften to eating temperature as you walk. The other draw is the mitarashi roll (¥580), a soft dango in a freshly cooked pancake with sweet-savory sauce, which one diner came back for; another wished for more sauce. Also red-bean-and-mochi and roasted-sweet-potato rolls. Mostly takeaway, with a bench by the door. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Japanese-sweets shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Wacaron (fresh dorayaki); mitarashi roll.

anecdotes.text: "It features a thin, soft dorayaki skin with a thick layer of cream in between. It was handed to us frozen solid, and after carrying it around… it melted to the perfect eating temperature." — August 2026, blueberry cheese cream ¥480.
"During my last visit to Osaka, I couldn't forget the deliciousness of the 'Mitara-shi Maki,' so I returned on this trip!" — August 2026.

Children and strollers welcome; takeout (Tabelog). Small lines form quickly at weekends (October 2026). Opened 29 April 2016 (Tabelog).
osaka_gufo_kitahorie.notes: [Sweets · featherlight soft serve and daily gelato, Kita-Horie] A glass-fronted ice cream shop near Yotsubashi with wood-and-white-tile decor, known for a soft serve so full of tiny air bubbles it eats like whipped cream. The milk flavor (¥420) is lightly sweet; seasonal ones like Japanese chestnut (¥540) and hazelnut taste strongly of the real thing, and portions are generous enough that one diner suggested sharing. The gelato case changes daily (¥420), with flavors such as salt vanilla, dried fig and cheese, pumpkin, hojicha and Earl Grey chocolate. There's a little eat-in space; weekend afternoons bring short lines. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Soft serve and gelato shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Airy soft serve; daily gelato.

anecdotes.text: "Compared to regular soft serve, it contains a lot of tiny air bubbles, making it incredibly light. You can also taste the rich chestnut flavor." — October 2026, Soft Serve Chestnut ¥540.
"The salt flavor was more pronounced than I expected, enhancing the sweetness of the vanilla. It was rich yet refreshing…" — October 2026, Salt Vanilla ¥420.

Order at the counter, then choose a seat (October 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Outlets and Wi-Fi; takeout (Tabelog). Opened 4 May 2026 (Tabelog).
osaka_obra_matcha_cafe_shinsaibashi.notes: [Café · an Uji-matcha café for dense pudding and gelato, Shinsaibashi] A calm, wood-accented matcha café near Shinsaibashi Station, opened May 2026 and open until 11 pm at weekends. The signature is a firm, rich Uji matcha pudding (¥900); add a scoop of the intensely bitter matcha gelato (+¥250) and a drizzle of matcha sauce. A matcha Basque cheesecake and a hojicha baked cheesecake are just as rich. Lattes are unsweetened, so the matcha comes through (the 'Zuiun' is ¥850), with mango and strawberry versions too. Diners call prices high and touristy, and one waited a long time, but matcha lovers rate it. Order first, then sit.

chef_bio.background: Matcha café (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Uji matcha pudding; matcha gelato.

anecdotes.text: "Pairing the dense and firm matcha pudding with the rich matcha gelato was simply the best! When I added matcha sauce, the matcha flavor intensified…" — October 2026, Uji Matcha Rich Pudding ¥900, gelato +¥250.
"The matcha latte had no syrup, allowing me to truly enjoy the authentic taste of matcha… Since it's priced for tourists, I hope it becomes a bit more affordable." — October 2026.

osaka_palm_cafe_creperie_horie.gf_detail: Ask. The shop says its galettes are made from buckwheat flour, water and salt only (Tabelog listing), but its crepes use French wheat flour and are cooked in the same kitchen; fillings and griddle sharing are not described.
osaka_palm_cafe_creperie_horie.vegan_detail: Ask. The galette batter is buckwheat, water and salt (Tabelog listing), but fillings use ham, cheese, egg and butter; no vegan filling is described.
osaka_palm_cafe_creperie_horie.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu, Sun, holidays and the day after 11:00–22:00 (last order 21:30); Wednesday 11:00–18:30; Friday, Saturday and the day before holidays 11:00–22:30 (Tabelog); closing days may vary. Reservations need a galette or crepe per person, not drinks only (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Non-smoking inside; e-cigarettes after 17:30; smoking on the terrace (Tabelog). Dogs welcome on the terrace, with crepes for dogs (Tabelog; August 2026). Order by QR code (August 2026).
osaka_palm_cafe_creperie_horie.notes: [Crêperie · buckwheat galettes and chewy crepes with a dog-friendly terrace, Kita-Horie] A wood-lined, Nordic-styled crêperie near Yotsubashi, open into the evening. Galettes are made from just buckwheat flour, water and salt; the Complete set (ham, cheese, egg, tomato, avocado and pesto, ¥1,900) changed one diner's view of galettes. The sweet crepes use French flour and Échiré butter, crisp at the edges and chewy, though one diner found the cream excessive. Order by QR at your table. Dogs are welcome on the terrace, and there are even crepes for them. Indoor seats are few, so book; reservations need food, not just drinks. Diners find the drinks pricey.

chef_bio.philosophy: Galettes of buckwheat flour, water and salt; crepes of French VIRON flour (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Buckwheat galettes; crepes.

"The atmosphere is nice, and the crepes are chewy and delicious, but there is just way too much whipped cream and cream!!!" — August 2026.

osaka_otto_coffee_sweets_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Daily 9:00–19:30; may change (Tabelog). No cards or e-money; PayPay accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking. A covered, terrace-like room facing Shinsaibashi-suji, air-conditioned (June 2026). Dog cookie add-on +¥250 (October 2026). Opened 19 March 2022 (Tabelog).
osaka_otto_coffee_sweets_shinsaibashi.notes: [Café · a bright café on the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade for pudding and seasonal sweets] A light, white café up a few steps from the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade, with a covered, terrace-like room facing the street that's a calm break from the crowds. Open from 9 am for brunch through evening. The pudding is firm and eggy with a slightly bitter caramel, and the seasonal menu goes all in: an autumn sweet-potato pudding with ice cream (¥780), a purple sweet-potato Mont Blanc mille-feuille layered with mochi and custard, a cinnamon sweet-potato tart. There's a sugar-butter crepe, soufflé cheesecake, and even tacos with a Corona. Coffee comes from a choice of two beans. Drinks from about ¥500. No cards or e-money; PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Café on Shinsaibashi-suji (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Pudding; seasonal sweets.

anecdotes.text: "The pudding had a nice, soft texture with a slightly bitter caramel, giving it a sophisticated touch." — August 2026.

"The purple sweet potato Mont Blanc mille-feuille… features mochi and custard layered within the flaky pastry, creating an indescribably delicious combination of chewy and crispy textures." — October 2026.

osaka_osaru_coffee_motomachi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the upstairs plates are sandwiches, croque monsieur, French toast, croissants and cheesecake.
osaka_osaru_coffee_motomachi.vegan_detail: Ask. Black coffee (Americano, iced dark roast) is on the menu; the food plates use egg, ham, cheese and béchamel.
osaka_osaru_coffee_motomachi.hours_raw: Daily 8:00–17:00; may change (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). Non-smoking; 11 seats; no reservations (Tabelog). The 1F stand serves coffee only; plates are served in the café on the 2F of the building next door (September 2026). About 15 people were waiting before the 8:00 opening on a Saturday, and the stairs fill with a line at busy times; don't line up in front of the neighboring Kumon (October 2026). Opened 22 August 2016 (Tabelog).
osaka_osaru_coffee_motomachi.notes: [Café · a dark-roast coffee stand with a busy breakfast café next door, Motomachi] A small specialty coffee spot a few minutes from JR Namba, open from 8 am every day. The ground-floor stand serves only coffee: a cozy wooden room with box seats where you take off your shoes, and coffees like the dark-roast 'Slow Boat' iced coffee, 'Magic Hour', a hot Ethiopian and a light, low-acid Americano. For food, go up to the café on the second floor of the building next door, where one diner had a creamy onion and bacon croque monsieur (¥1,400) with a dark hot coffee (¥700) and another a ham and egg sandwich plate with a well-dressed salad and honey yogurt. Expect a line: about 15 people were waiting before opening one Saturday, and the line runs up the stairs; don't queue in front of the Kumon next door. When the stand is busy, orders can take a while.

chef_bio.background: Specialty coffee stand with a separate café upstairs next door (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Dark-roast coffee; croque monsieur and sandwich plates.

anecdotes.text: "The Croque Monsieur was generously filled with béchamel sauce, cheese, bacon, and onions. It was creamy, with the sweetness of the onions perfectly balancing the saltiness of the bacon." — October 2026, Onion and Bacon Croque Monsieur ¥1,400.
"The first floor serves only coffee, while the second floor offers plates with croissants, Croque Monsieur, French toast, and cheesecake. The entrance was a bit hard to find!" — September 2026.

osaka_over_the_over_nambanaka.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options; a grilled vegetable salad is on the à la carte menu, but the course dishes described use fish, meat or cheese.

Sofa seats are first-come even with a reservation (August 2026). Opened 16 April 2018 (Tabelog).
osaka_over_the_over_nambanaka.notes: [Creative · natural wine and seasonal plates from an open kitchen, Namba] A wood-toned second-floor restaurant beside the railway near Nankai Namba, open until midnight, where the cooking is ingredient-led and the wine list leans natural. Courses (from ¥8,000, plus an anniversary course) run from a playful 'American dog' in jet-black binchotan-charcoal batter to buri carpaccio, charcoal-grilled sawara, a sweet-potato soup with stracciatella, sansho Bolognese and low-temperature Kyoto Hiyoshi pork, ending with black figs and canelé. You can also go à la carte: crab miso toast, a porcini omelette, grilled vegetable salad and a pork sauté that won over one seafood eater. Good non-alcoholic drinks too. It suits celebrations, and a birthday plate can be arranged. Sofa seats are first-come even if you've booked. Table charge ¥550. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredient-led dishes with natural wine (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal course; charcoal-grilled meat and fish.

anecdotes.text: "The batter was mixed with binchotan charcoal, and inside was spiced meat." — October 2026, American Dog on the anniversary course.
"I usually eat seafood, but the pork sauté here completely changed my perception. It was the first time I truly enjoyed a pork sauté." — August 2026.

osaka_mill_pour_minamisenba.notes: [Café · a specialty coffee stand with a roadside bench, Minami-Senba] A tiny coffee stand east of Shinsaibashi with two seats inside and a tented bench along the road outside. The coffee is the point: a piping-hot, rich long black, a refreshing low-acid cold brew (M ¥750), Americanos and a creamy iced latte, with beans to take home. There's a hot dog if you're hungry. Look carefully, as the sign is small next to its neighbors. Smoking is allowed on the terrace, which one diner found uncomfortable. No credit cards; e-money and QR are fine. Weekday hours are 9 am–6 pm; check weekend hours, which the listing gives two ways.

chef_bio.background: Specialty coffee stand (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Long black; cold brew; coffee beans.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered a hot long black coffee. It was piping hot and quite rich in flavor, with a strong aroma." — February 2026.
"It has some bitterness but is refreshing, with almost no acidity. This is easy to drink—delicious coffee!" — June 2026, Black Cold Brew (M) ¥750.

osaka_potto_meat_sauce_minamisenba.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a pasta shop serving wheat fresh pasta or whole-wheat pasta; no gluten-free pasta mentioned.
osaka_potto_meat_sauce_minamisenba.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: meat sauces, cream sauces and carbonara; arrabbiata is listed but no vegan pasta is described.

No lunch reservations; dinner reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR (PayPay) accepted (Tabelog). 18 seats: 12 at the counter, 6 on the terrace; smoking and pets only on the terrace (Tabelog). QR ordering (October 2026). Opened 4 March 2013 (Tabelog).
osaka_potto_meat_sauce_minamisenba.notes: [Pasta · homemade meat sauce on chewy fresh pasta, Minami-Senba] A small counter pasta shop near Shinsaibashi built around its meat sauce, slow-simmered from the beef cut senbon-suji. The classic version is rich and clings well to chewy fresh pasta without any meaty smell; the listing also highlights a cream meat sauce with Australian grain-fed beef meatballs, and there are limited sauces like a dashi meat sauce topped with bonito flakes, a monthly avocado cream, carbonara and arrabbiata. Choose fresh or whole-wheat noodles. Weekday lunch includes a free large size and a side of soup, and drinks are just +¥200. Ordering is by QR code. One diner found the oyster and karasumi pasta bland and disliked being pushed to add the shop on LINE. Six terrace seats allow smoking and pets.

chef_bio.background: Pasta shop specializing in homemade meat sauce (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Meat sauce slow-simmered from senbon-suji beef (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Homemade meat sauce; chewy fresh pasta.

anecdotes.text: "The noodles were chewy, and the sauce was rich and well-coated, making it delicious. It was a traditional meat sauce without any overpowering meat smell…" — October 2026, classic meat sauce with fresh pasta.
"It was topped with bonito flakes, giving it a lovely Japanese flavor, and it was incredibly delicious! The noodles were wonderfully chewy!" — September 2026, limited-time dashi meat sauce.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 自家製ミートソース potto、大阪市中央区南船場3-6-1 サイプレス心斎橋 1F、心斎橋駅2番出口から徒歩3分、平日11:00〜15:00・17:00〜22:00、土日祝11:00〜22:00、不定休あり、ランチの予約不可、カード (VISA・Master・JCB・AMEX・Diners)・電子マネー・QR (PayPay) 可、18席 (カウンター12席、テラス6席)、喫煙とペットはテラスのみ、2013年3月4日開店、公式サイトあり。店の紹介: senbon-suji をじっくり煮込んだ自家製ミートソース、オーストラリア産のグレインフェッドの牛100%のミートボールとクリームミートソース、カルボナーラ、アラビアータ。口コミ(2026年9〜10月): 期間限定のだしミートソース (かつお節のせ)、もちもちの生パスタ、全粒粉の麺も選べる、今月のアボカドクリーム、平日ランチは大盛り無料でスープつき、ドリンク+200円、QRで注文、牡蠣と karasumi のパスタは karasumi の味が薄く、接客が一方的でLINEの友だち登録を求められたという声。

osaka_yamasantei_shinmachi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; Sichuan dishes such as mapo tofu usually use soy sauce or bean pastes, and the menu includes noodles, dumplings and spring rolls.
osaka_yamasantei_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: set meals center on mapo tofu with meat, fried chicken, pork and shrimp; no vegan dish described.
osaka_yamasantei_shinmachi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:00 and 17:30–21:00; Saturday 11:00–15:00, with Saturday dinner only by reservation for two or more; closed Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). 16 seats with a counter and a table in the back; designated smoking area (Tabelog). Every lunch set is ¥1,000, with two pieces of fried chicken +¥200 (Tabelog listing). Set meals are also served at night (September–October 2026). Opened 22 May 2023 (Tabelog).
osaka_yamasantei_shinmachi.notes: [Chinese · numbing Sichuan mapo tofu and set meals, Yotsubashi] A small, calm Sichuan eatery in the basement of a building you reach straight from Yotsubashi Station's Exit 2 stairs. The owner formerly ran Meigen, a popular Chinese restaurant in Honmachi, so its signature mapo tofu lives on here; the listing also cites experience at Osaka's Koshin. Every lunch set is ¥1,000, and mapo tofu is the house signature: boldly Sichuan, with a generous hit of numbing pepper that one diner calls addictive and another found too spicy to finish. Unusually, set meals continue at night, like a ¥1,500 two-item platter of mapo tofu and yurinchi with refillable soup and rice. In the evening there are small plates for drinking too: dry dandan noodles (small ¥500), steamed chicken with Hong Kong sauce (¥300), a spicy shrimp mayo and century egg tofu with sesame sauce. One person runs the place, so expect to wait a little for orders. Closed Sundays; Saturday dinner is by reservation only.

chef_bio.background: Sichuan Chinese eatery (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner formerly ran Meigen, a popular Chinese restaurant in Honmachi, so its signature mapo tofu lives on here; the listing also cites experience at Osaka's Koshin (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Mapo tofu; dry dandan noodles; set meals.

anecdotes.text: "The Mapo Tofu is boldly Sichuan-style with a tolerable level of spiciness, and the shrimp omelet (instead of crab) was really to my liking." — September 2026.
"The Dan Dan Noodles here have a simple yet delicious flavor that's quite addictive. At JPY 500, it's a great deal." — October 2026, Dan Dan Noodles without soup (small) ¥500.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 山三亭、大阪市西区新町1-5-7 四ツ橋ビルディング B1F、四ツ橋駅2番出口の改札を出て左の階段を上がる、四ツ橋駅から124m、月〜金11:00〜15:00・17:30〜21:00、土11:00〜15:00 (土曜の夜は2名以上の予約のみ)、日祝休み、予約可、カード・電子マネー・QR可、16席、分煙、2023年5月22日開店、Instagramあり。店の紹介: 本格四川料理、看板は mapo tofu と yodare-dori、ランチは全品1000円で kara-age 2個を+200円、夜は90分の飲み放題つきのコース2種。口コミ(2026年7〜10月): mapo tofu の定食 (花椒がたっぷりで辛くしびれる、辛すぎて食べきれなかったという声も)、炒飯の定食 (yurinchi 2個つき)、夜も定食あり、2品盛りの定食1500円 (mapo tofu、yurinchi、漬物、スープはおかわり自由、ご飯はおかわり1回無料)、汁なし担々麺 (小) 500円、香港ソースの蒸し鶏300円、ピリ辛のエビマヨ (小) 500円、ピータン豆腐のごまソース、エビの玉子焼き、酢豚、エビチリ、春巻き、 shumai、 xiao long bao、ひとりで切り盛りしているので注文と提供に少し時間がかかる。

osaka_patisserie_accueil_kitahorie.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; cakes are mostly mousse-based but include sponge, roll cake and kouign-amann.
osaka_patisserie_accueil_kitahorie.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: cream, mascarpone and chocolate mousse cakes; no vegan cake described.
osaka_patisserie_accueil_kitahorie.hours_raw: Wed–Sun 11:00–19:00; closed Monday and Tuesday; may change (Tabelog). Cake orders can be reserved by phone; the eat-in seats cannot be reserved (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). 4 counter seats for eat-in; non-smoking; takeout; children welcome (Tabelog). Opened 13 June 2014 (Tabelog).
osaka_patisserie_accueil_kitahorie.notes: [Sweets · light mousse cakes and chocolate, Kita-Horie] A small, stylish patisserie a minute from Nishi-Ohashi Station, with a showcase of seasonal cakes and just four counter seats to eat in. One diner notes that most cakes are mousse-based and made airy, so fruit and chocolate come through without heaviness: the Écrin (¥700) layers strawberry and mascarpone mousse around a passion fruit centre, and one diner compared its texture to a premium Aero bar. In autumn there is a chestnut roll (roulé au marron, ¥680) with Hokkaido cream and a Japanese-chestnut Mont Blanc; the soufflé au chocolat (¥680) is surprisingly light. Kouign-amann to take away, and café au lait (¥600) or a creamy cappuccino to drink. Eat-in seats can't be booked, so come soon after the 11:00 opening; cakes can be reserved by phone. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Patisserie and chocolatier (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Light mousse cakes; chocolate; seasonal fruit cakes.

anecdotes.text: "When you take a fork to it, the mousse is surprisingly light, filled with air… The tang of the passion fruit adds a refreshing kick, ensuring the sweetness doesn't overwhelm." — October 2026, Écrin ¥700.

"The sponge cake was moist and chewy, paired with Hokkaido cream and chestnut chantilly… The soufflé chocolate was surprisingly light and easy to eat, despite being chocolate." — October 2026, Roulé au Marron ¥680, Soufflé au Chocolat ¥680.

osaka_honeysuckle_rose_minamisenba.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the daily plate changes and has included croquettes, tempura, udon and a hamburg steak with ponzu.

No cards, no e-money and no QR payments (Tabelog). No reservations; 20 seats; smoking allowed (Tabelog). Drinks after lunch may not be available when busy (March 2025).
osaka_honeysuckle_rose_minamisenba.notes: [Café · a retro tea room with a home-style daily lunch plate, Minami-Senba] A dimly lit café near Nagahoribashi that feels like an old Western-style house or British tea room, with antique furniture and stained glass. A reviewer describes it as run by a lovely elderly couple. It opens only Tuesday to Thursday for lunch and serves one thing: the daily 'Honeysuckle rice' plate (¥1,100, ¥1,300 with a drink), a main such as a light Japanese-style hamburg steak with grated daikon and ponzu plus several small vegetable sides, white or mixed-grain rice and soup. Several diners value it as a balanced, home-style meal that changes every day; a mini parfait or cake can be added. One diner was served hot water on arrival in winter. Cash only, and smoking is allowed inside.

chef_bio.background: Tea-room café serving a daily lunch plate (Tabelog; 2023–2026 reviews). A reviewer describes it as run by a lovely elderly couple (January 2023 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Daily "Honeysuckle rice" lunch plate.

anecdotes.text: "The Hamburg steak seemed to be a mix of meats, mostly chicken mince. It was served with a grated daikon sauce and chopped perilla leaves, making it light and delicious." — February 2026, Honeysuckle Rice ¥1,100.
"The main dish, a Hamburg steak, came with three side dishes that were delicious and well-seasoned." — March 2025.

osaka_gelamu_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: milk-based gelato such as latte, pistachio and matcha; mango and strawberry may be sorbets but nothing is labeled dairy-free.

Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR (PayPay, d Barai, au PAY, Alipay, WeChat Pay) accepted (Tabelog). 10 seats and an open terrace; dogs welcome inside; takeout and delivery; children and strollers welcome (Tabelog). No tasting spoons (August–October 2026). Opened 12 July 2025 (Tabelog).
osaka_gelamu_shinsaibashi.notes: [Sweets · late-night gelato, Minami-Senba] A clean, elegant gelato shop between Shinsaibashi and Nagahoribashi, open until 10 pm, which makes it a handy dessert stop after dinner. One diner called the gelato natural, another found flavors not seen elsewhere: tangy mango, café latte, latte noir, pistachio, matcha, Earl Grey, strawberry and walnut, with the DUO giving two in a cone. One diner had the Earl Grey Blanc (¥1,300), full of bergamot aroma; there's a matcha affogato too. There are no tasting spoons, so decide at the case. Dogs are welcome inside, and there's a small terrace. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Gelato shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Gelato; late opening.

anecdotes.text: "The moment I took a bite, the aroma of bergamot filled my nose, and the sweetness was just right—delicious!" — August 2026, Earl Grey Blanc ¥1,300.
"The Latte Noir and Pistachio I tried were both rich yet refreshing, and absolutely delicious!" — October 2026.

osaka_salon_de_the_plaisir_minamihorie.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; parfaits come with crumbles and brûlée, and the afternoon tea includes sandwiches and scones.
osaka_salon_de_the_plaisir_minamihorie.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: parfaits are built on milk gelato, custard and cream; sandwiches use cream cheese and duck.
osaka_salon_de_the_plaisir_minamihorie.hours_raw: Wed–Sun 12:00–20:00; closed Monday and Tuesday; open on holiday Mondays with the next day off; check Instagram for changes (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). No cards, no e-money and no QR payments (Tabelog). 14 seats, seven tables for two; groups up to 4; non-smoking (Tabelog; September 2026). Every guest, children included, orders at least one food item; parfaits come as a drink set, and drinks over ¥800 cost ¥100 or more extra (September 2026). Opened 24 March 2014 (Tabelog).
osaka_salon_de_the_plaisir_minamihorie.notes: [Café · seasonal fruit parfaits and pot tea, Minami-Horie] A small European-style tea salon facing Minami-Horie Park, known for elaborate seasonal fruit parfaits: peach Melba with a whole peach in summer, melon, blood orange or ruby grapefruit with brûlée, Shine Muscat and grape in autumn (¥2,600, or ¥2,900 with a drink). The owner-chef, who makes the seasonal desserts, is from France. One diner swapped in the deep-steamed sencha gelato (+¥50) and found it lighter than matcha. The tea list is long and comes by the pot. For a fuller visit, the afternoon tea set adds sandwiches (the cream cheese is the star for one diner), scones and a dessert; crepes with pistachio ice cream sell out some days. House rules: each guest orders at least one food item, parfaits come as a drink set, and pricier drinks cost extra. One diner found the bowls smaller than in the photos. Cash only; reservations taken; closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Salon de thé serving seasonal parfaits, sandwiches and tea (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). The owner-chef, who makes the seasonal desserts, is from France (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal fruit parfaits; tea by the pot.

anecdotes.text: "The combination of vanilla ice cream and the tartness of raspberries made for a parfait that was enjoyable until the very last bite." — July 2026, Peach Melba-style Parfait.

osaka_motti_cafe_nambanaka.notes: [Café · a bright, all-white dessert café, Namba-naka] A tiny, photogenic café on a residential street south of Namba, white from floor to ceiling with rounded tables and chairs. Desserts are the draw: a white chocolate cheese terrine that's refreshingly cheesy with a milky finish, a chocolate terrine and brownies, plus limited fruit fairs such as a lemon month with honey-drizzled lemon cake (¥890) and lemonade (¥800). Drinks include a strawberry milk soda with fruit pieces, royal milk tea and an aromatic café au lait, and a message can be added to an order. Seats are close together and there can be a short wait outside. Open from 9 am, until 8 pm on Fridays; closing days vary.
